fgisu.summary: Requests, contracts and cloud resource consumption tracking for government information systems.
fgisu.description: The federal information system “Management of the Unified State Cloud Platform” connects an agency’s computing needs with approvals, contracts and service provision. The government customer is Russia’s Ministry of Digital Development, Communications and Mass Media.
fgisu.audience: The system manages the government cloud: agencies request resources for their information systems, suppliers manage service provision, and the regulator reviews requirements and monitors usage.
fgisu.role: Designed the microservice architecture and developed services with Node.js and NestJS. Wrote code for backend services, integrations and account interfaces. Responsible for business process automation with Zeebe and the contract microservice; maintained a shared service library.

brief.task: Connect agency requests, contract terms, infrastructure and actual cloud service consumption within a shared workflow.
brief.solution: Approval automation with Zeebe, microservices and shared rules for exchanging data, connected to account interfaces, resource records and analytics.
brief.result: A resource requirement passes through approval and becomes the basis for an order. Participants can track its status, agreed volumes and resource usage.

sources.customer: Public information about the government customer

context.title: Who uses the system and why
context.description: Cloud resources support government information systems, budgets and contractual obligations. Participants need to know who requested computing capacity, the terms of provision and how it is used. The system brings these records and workflows together.

consumer.title: Consumer agency
consumer.description: Defines its information system’s computing, storage and other service requirements. Tracks approvals, orders and consumption.

supplier.title: Resource supplier
supplier.description: Works with services, contract terms and orders. Matches requested volumes to available infrastructure.

regulator.title: Regulator and analyst
regulator.description: Review requirements, take part in approvals and analyse resource usage. Reports help compare ordered volumes with actual consumption.

workflow.title: From a request to consumption tracking
workflow.description: An agency needs additional resources for its information system. It submits a request and agrees its contents; the approved volumes then form the basis for orders. After services are provided, the system helps track usage. Select a step for details.

contribution.title: My contribution
contribution.description: Designed microservice interactions and implemented them in code. My main responsibilities were business process automation with Zeebe, the contract service and a shared service library. I also developed requests, resource records, reporting and account interfaces.

zeebe.title: Zeebe and business processes
zeebe.description: Developed the Zeebe integration, business process diagrams and task handlers. Connected approvals, revision requests, reminders and stage transitions to actions in the account interface.

contracts.title: Contract microservice
contracts.description: Developed the contract microservice and its integrations: services and pricing, volume limits, consumer access, attachments, invoices and service quality terms.

common.title: Shared service library
common.description: Maintained the shared library: data exchange between services, data structures, access checks and Zeebe integration. Shared modules were used across the system’s services.

requests.title: Requests and resource records
requests.description: Developed the request service and its processes. Extended the infrastructure inventory (CMDB): request versions, approved resource sets and links between volumes and orders. Worked on technical support processes.

frontend.title: Account interfaces and integrations
frontend.description: Extended the Nuxt/Vue portal’s account overview for each user role, consumption forecasts and technical support. Developed the shared entry point for interface requests (API gateway) and data exchange with services.

analytics.title: Reports and documents
analytics.description: Worked on reporting services, Cube.js models, the report builder interface and government agency IT resource records. Extended document generation, file storage and the change log.

system.title: Microservices with clear responsibilities
system.description: The account interface sends requests to a shared entry point: the API gateway. Node.js and NestJS services handle requests, resources and contracts, while Zeebe manages approvals and participants’ tasks. Select a block to learn its role.

coordination.title: Keeping decisions and resources consistent
coordination.description: A single request brings together the agency, supplier and regulator. Resource requirements can change during approval. The system needs to preserve the agreed version, offer each participant the right actions and carry the approved volumes into the order.

versions.title: Requirement versions
versions.description: Revised requirements must preserve the approved resource set. Saved versions connect participants’ decisions to specific resources.

permissions.title: Roles and access
permissions.description: Consumers, suppliers and regulators work with the same request but have different actions available. Access checks apply in the interface and on the server.

handoff.title: Long-running approvals
handoff.description: A process waits for a human decision, returns a request for revision and resumes after a response. Zeebe stores its state and assigns work to task handlers.

traceability.title: Connection to orders
traceability.description: Requests, selected resources, services and orders are linked. The change log records actions, while notifications keep participants informed.

analytics.title: Ordered resources and actual consumption
analytics.description: Work continues after approval: participants need to see how the supplied capacity is used. Analytics combines resource records and metrics for reports and consumption forecasts. The report builder offers measures, groupings and filters; the document generator produces forms and exports.

fgisu.architecture: The backend uses Node.js, NestJS and TypeScript. The API gateway accepts interface requests and routes them to the appropriate microservice. Services exchange data through gRPC, a protocol that lets one service call functions in another. A shared service library provides data structures, data exchange modules and access checks.
fgisu.constraints: Zeebe manages approvals and long-running business processes: assigns tasks, waits for decisions and moves requests to the next stage. RabbitMQ and WebSocket deliver notifications so participants can see changes in their accounts.
fgisu.implementation: Nuxt and Vue power account interfaces; PostgreSQL stores business data; ClickHouse and Cube.js serve analytics and forecasts. Separate services generate documents and handle files in MinIO/S3.

powersketch.summary: Web editor for electrical diagrams with an equipment library, reports and document export.
powersketch.description: PowerSketch lets an electrician build a panel much as they would at a workbench: choose real devices from the catalog, place them on the diagram, and connect them with wires. The service then creates the device list and connection table automatically, so nothing has to be copied by hand.
powersketch.audience: It is made for electricians, smart-home integrators, panel builders, commissioning engineers, and technical specialists.
powersketch.role: I build PowerSketch end to end: user flows, interface and data design, frontend, backend, production releases, and ongoing product support.
powersketch.approach: The diagram sits at the center of the editor. Every device has dimensions and pins, every wire has two endpoints, and every layer has an order and visibility. Change something once and the update appears in the editor, reports, and exported file.
powersketch.architecture: Diagram editing happens in the browser, so every move feels immediate. The server stores projects and the catalog and handles sign-in, shared links, and subscriptions. The user never has to think about that split—they can simply continue where they left off.
powersketch.systemTitle: One diagram, all the data you need
powersketch.constraints: Large diagrams still need to feel smooth, and an exported file needs to match what users see in the editor. Older projects must keep opening after updates, and the core tools need to work across different screen sizes.

workflow.description: Every step is connected. The user draws the diagram once, and PowerSketch reuses that information for reports, sharing, and export.

customDevices.description: Enter its dimensions, upload an image, and place the pins. PNG, JPG, SVG, and WEBP files up to 5 MB are supported. A new model can also be suggested for the shared catalog.

reports.title: Reports are built from the diagram
reports.description: One report lists device models, specifications, notes, and quantities. Another lists every wire with its label, cross-section, length, source, and destination. Unneeded columns can be removed before download.

handoff.title: The result is easy to review and hand off
handoff.description: Send a view-only link to a colleague or client—no account or editor access is required. For installation or printing, export the diagram as SVG with the right background, paper size, and orientation.

productModel.description: The editor and device catalog are included in the free plan. Plus and Professional suit people managing more projects, with higher limits, project copying, and watermark-free export.

planesArch.audience: The website introduces the studio to future clients and gives architects and designers a way to discover PLANES educational programs.
planesArch.role: I handled the interface and responsive build, set up the CMS (admin panel), implemented Russian and English versions, added filters, galleries, and display themes, and prepared the website for launch.
planesArch.architecture: The studio manages projects, copy, and photography through the CMS (admin panel), without touching code. Content appears on the website in the right language, while photography adapts to the screen.
planesArch.constraints: The main constraints were the weight of project galleries, the different lengths of Russian and English copy, and the need to preserve a balanced layout on phones, tablets, and wide screens.

cnp.summary: A media content management system for preparing meetings and controlling a video wall from a tablet.
cnp.description: The Media Content Management System was developed for the Analytical Center for the Government of the Russian Federation and is used at the Government Coordination Center. It connects meeting preparation with live display control: documents, video, cameras, web applications and dashboards can be shown on a large video wall.
cnp.audience: Operators, speakers and specialists preparing meetings, presentations and analytical materials for the Coordination Center.
cnp.role: Designed the architecture of the entire system and developed the backend, operator web console and Electron application for displaying content on the video wall.

brief.task: Give operators convenient control over different materials on a video wall during meetings and presentations.
brief.solution: Designed the system architecture and developed the backend, tablet operator console and Electron application for displaying content on the video wall.
brief.result: Preparation and live display form one workflow: operators choose materials and control the screen from a tablet.

deployment.title: From the operator’s tablet to a government meeting room
deployment.description: The project’s working environment is the Government Coordination Center. Presentations, documents, video calls and indicators share a room, with content and layouts that operators can change as the meeting progresses.

system.title: How the system fits together
system.description: The operator uses a tablet. The server connects their actions with materials and the display system, while a player sends the selected content to the video wall. The current display state returns to the console.

workflow.title: From meeting preparation to the room display
workflow.description: Materials and the presentation sequence are prepared in advance. During the meeting, the operator switches episodes, controls individual screen areas and sees the display state in the console.

complexity.title: What has to come together behind one operator action
complexity.description: Selecting a material on a tablet coordinates several applications, different sources and independent areas of a large screen.

sources.title: Different sources in one display
sources.description: Documents, video, cameras, web pages and updating widgets need different loading, viewing and control methods.

sync.title: The console shares the screen’s state
sync.description: Commands pass through the server, while the screen state returns to the operator: the active scenario, material pages, audio and timers.

layouts.title: Each area has its own content
layouts.description: The large screen is divided into areas and columns. Materials can have their own pages, playlist order and playback duration.

access.title: Clear control over the display
access.description: Roles and permissions determine access to materials and actions. Operators can hand control to one another.

interface.title: A closer look at the operator console
interface.description: The console brings together scenarios, the material library, screen layouts and display controls. The images below show the interface with demo content.

cnp.architecture: The operator console, administration panel and display player share one server. The HTTP API handles material uploads and scenario changes, while Socket.IO carries control commands and the current display state. The server checks permissions and connects users and screens belonging to each venue.
cnp.constraints: Touch controls need to remain clear while several materials are open on the video wall. Document pages, video, audio and timers share the display state. When several operators are working, roles, permissions and control handover determine who can change the screen content.
cnp.implementation: The operator console uses Nuxt, Vue, Vuex and Vuetify; the administration panel uses React. A NestJS server with TypeORM and PostgreSQL stores materials, scenarios and access settings. Redis and Bull queues handle background data updates and material processing. The Electron, Nuxt and Vue display player receives commands and shows content in the specified screen areas.

operator.title: Operator console
operator.summary: Preparation and control from a tablet
operator.detail: The operator builds a scenario, selects materials and controls the display: switching episodes and pages, and working with video, audio and timers.

sources.title: Materials and data
sources.detail: The library contains different material types. Widgets receive data from connected sources, while documents and media are used in scenarios and layouts.

server.title: System server
server.detail: The server stores scenarios and material information, checks user permissions and passes commands between the console and the display system.

player.title: Player
player.detail: The display application receives selected content and control commands, places materials in screen areas and reports the display state.

wall.title: Video wall
wall.summary: A shared screen for the meeting
wall.detail: Selected materials appear on the large screen. Several areas can show, for example, a presentation, a document and a dashboard at the same time.

prepare.title: Prepare
prepare.summary: Gather materials and build a scenario
prepare.detail: Before a meeting, materials can be selected from the library, episodes placed in order and speaker notes prepared for the teleprompter.

select.title: Select
select.summary: Open the right episode on the tablet
select.detail: During the meeting, the operator selects a scenario or episode and controls materials in individual screen areas.

deliver.title: Display
deliver.summary: Send a command to the video wall
deliver.detail: The server passes the command to the display system. The player shows materials in the chosen layout and carries out playback commands.

confirm.title: See the state
confirm.detail: The console receives screen state, including the active scenario, pages, audio and timers. This gives the operator context for their next action.
